summary: Round 2 confirms that Decisions 9, 11, 8, and 12 respectively close the valid mixed-layout replay blocker, misleading record INFO, silent terminal-exposure widening, and acceptance-evidence secret-handling gap. Decision 10 now specifies the required dedicated-cluster ownership, targeted PASS, concurrency exclusion, safety margin, and object/configuration cleanup, but one safety-critical binding remains unspecified: the existing test connector always targets the shared PG19 endpoint, and the marker is not contractually bound to either an injected dedicated endpoint or whole-test network isolation. The pre-existing malformed-archive Ncols crash remains out of scope.

findings.category: A05 - destructive fixture isolation is not bound to the connection target
findings.title: The dedicated-cluster marker can still authorize XID and autovacuum mutations against the shared PG19 fixture
findings.description: Decision 10 makes execution conditional on an external dedicated-cluster marker, but does not specify how the test connection is redirected to that dedicated cluster or require the targeted test process to run inside the dedicated cluster's isolated container/network namespace. The established connector ignores any marker and always connects to 127.0.0.1:21919, database pgcenter_fixtures, user postgres. Consequently, an implementation can satisfy the literal marker/timeout/cleanup requirements while the harness creates a disposable PG19 on another port and the test still burns XIDs and runs ALTER SYSTEM against the ordinary shared fixture. 'No concurrent packages' reduces interference but does not make mutation of the wrong cluster safe. Accident vector: a harness supplies the marker and starts a dedicated instance on a nonstandard endpoint, while the test uses NewTestConnectVersion(190000) unchanged; the destructive operations hit the shared instance and the harness later destroys only the unused dedicated one. No harness exists yet, so this is a verified design/contract gap rather than a claim about an observed runtime incident.
findings.evidence: Read-only source inspection confirms NewTestConnectVersion has a fixed 190000→21919 mapping and calls NewConfig with fixed host/database/user; neither it nor NewConfig reads a dedicated-cluster endpoint variable. Repository-wide search found no endpoint override in the internal test helpers. Searches of Decision 10 and its testing/data-map derivatives found a marker but no requirement for endpoint injection, same-network-namespace execution, or a preflight endpoint-identity assertion. Glob also confirms the future acceptance/harness directory is not present yet, so no unseen implementation currently resolves the binding.
findings.recommendation: Make the connection target part of Decision 10's safety contract. Either (a) require the entire targeted go-test process to run in the dedicated disposable container/network namespace where 127.0.0.1:21919 is necessarily the single-use PG19 and no shared fixture is reachable, or (b) give the test a test-only host/port/database configuration supplied by the harness instead of using the fixed helper. In both cases require a preflight server-identity/disposable-marker assertion immediately before ALTER SYSTEM/XID burn and fail closed if it does not match. Keep the surviving external owner/supervisor responsible for cluster destruction after test timeout or SIGKILL, and retain the specified no-concurrency, targeted-PASS, object cleanup, autovacuum restoration, and freeze-margin checks.

findings.category: CWE-20/CWE-129 - malformed recorded archive denial of service
findings.title: Archive-controlled Ncols remains unvalidated; Decision 9 intentionally covers only valid layouts
findings.description: PGresult.validate still checks each decoded row against len(Cols) and Nrows against the decoded row count, but does not require Ncols==len(Cols). A small crafted archive can declare an excessive Ncols with otherwise consistent columns/rows. On a diffed screen, diff then loops to attacker-controlled curr.Ncols and indexes both current and previous row slices beyond their actual widths, causing an index-out-of-range panic. Attack vector: an operator replays an untrusted downloaded or replaced tar. Decision 9 correctly states that it handles valid adjacent column layouts, not attacker-declared malformed Ncols, so this pre-existing issue is not a feature 018 blocker and must not be counted as a regression in the new replay work.
findings.evidence: Read-only inspection confirms validate still lacks the Ncols/Cols equality check and diff still uses `for l := 0; l < curr.Ncols; l++` before indexing row values. Debt [020] records prior reproduction of the malformed-shape panic. Read-only command `go test ./report -run 'Test_processData_versionChange|Test_app_doReport_errorPathDoesNotHang' -count=1 -v` passed the existing valid-version-change and error-drain tests; those tests do not assert malformed Ncols rejection. Decision 8 explicitly excludes attacker-declared malformed Ncols from Decision 9.
findings.recommendation: Track separately under debt [020]: reject negative/implausible dimensions, require Ncols==len(Cols), validate all consumer indices and adjacent-layout compatibility before diff/alignment, and return a descriptive report error instead of panicking. Add malformed-archive tests for oversized/undersized Ncols, invalid row shapes, and invalid sort/unique keys. Do not use SC-10's valid-layout evidence as proof that this untrusted-input class is fixed.
